rubrics.justification: The response appropriately identifies a transfer-quality expanded blastocyst consistent with 3AB, notes a visible ICM and relatively loose/nonuniform TE, and comments on zona thinning. It is somewhat cautious and generally accurate, though a few statements (e.g., absence of degeneration/multinucleation) go beyond what can be confidently determined from a single image.

It integrates age-related aneuploidy risk, prior miscarriage, ovarian reserve, sperm parameters, BMI, endometrium, and lifestyle factors well, and explains how these modify prognosis despite decent morphology.

The reasoning is structured and mostly consistent, especially around morphology versus age-related aneuploidy. Minor issues include some overlap/confusion between implantation and clinical pregnancy ranges and a slightly optimistic probability framing relative to the stated risks.

Recommendations are broadly evidence-based: single embryo transfer, avoidance of unproven add-ons, smoking cessation, and cautious discussion of PGT-A. Small limitations include somewhat broad prognostic estimates and not explicitly distinguishing fresh versus frozen transfer implications.

The response gives practical next steps for transfer, lifestyle optimization, luteal support, and future-cycle considerations including PGT-A discussion and further evaluation if failures continue. It is useful, though not highly tailored in protocol-level detail.
